origin.description: Importance sampling weights that correct for simulation from probabilities p when estimates are wanted under probabilities q.

arguments.name: boot.out
arguments.text: A boot object from boot or tilt.boot. The replicates are usually drawn with unequal probabilities.

arguments.name: def
arguments.text: If true, and the replicates were drawn under more than one distribution, use a defensive mixture of those distributions. A single distribution always uses the distribution that produced each replicate.

arguments.name: q
arguments.text: Probabilities for the resampling distribution under which inferences are required. The default gives equal weight to each observation. Every element must be positive, and the length is the number of observations.

origin.details: The weight of a replicate with frequency vector f is prod((q/p)^f). When R has several values, def = TRUE mixes the sampling distributions in proportion to the number of replicates from each one. def = FALSE uses the distribution that produced that replicate. The frequencies are the matrix boot.array rebuilds for the bootstrap.
origin.value: A numeric vector of weights, one per replicate, with the same length as the bootstrap replicates.
origin.example:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(boot))
set.seed(1)
x <- c(10, 12, 9, 15, 11, 14)
weights <- c(0.05, 0.15, 0.1, 0.3, 0.25, 0.15)
statistic <- function(d, w) sum(d * w) / sum(w)
b <- boot(x, statistic, R = 12, stype = "w", weights = weights)
print(imp.weights(b))

translation.description: Importance sampling weights that correct for simulation from probabilities p when estimates are wanted under probabilities q.

arguments.name: boot_out
arguments.text: Bootstrap object with t, t0, data, weights, strata, R, and frequency. weights are the resampling probabilities p. frequency is the resample count matrix copied from boot.array for that same bootstrap. strata uses the numeric codes of the R strata.

arguments.name: def_
arguments.text: This is def in R. If true, and R has more than one value, use a defensive mixture of the sampling distributions. A single value of R always uses the distribution that produced each replicate.

arguments.name: q
arguments.text: Probabilities for the resampling distribution under which inferences are required. None gives equal weight to each observation. Every element must be positive, and the length is the number of observations.

translation.details: The weight of a replicate with frequency vector f is prod((q/p)^f). When R has several values, def_ = True mixes the sampling distributions in proportion to the number of replicates from each one. def_ = False uses the distribution that produced that replicate. The frequency matrix is read from the object. This function does not redraw the resamples.
translation.value: A NumPy vector of weights, one per replicate.
